pa_facts.claim: Under 15 Pa.C.S. § 146(a) (added by Act 122 of 2022), every domestic filing entity, domestic limited liability partnership, domestic electing partnership that is not a limited partnership, and registered foreign association must file an annual report with the Department of State.
pa_facts.quote: (a) Required contents.--A domestic filing entity, domestic limited liability partnership, domestic electing partnership that is not a limited partnership or registered foreign association must deliver to the department for filing an annual report signed by the entity or association that states:
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 146. Annual report (PA General Assembly)

pa_facts.claim: DOS lists the entities that must file: domestic business corporations, nonprofit corporations, LLCs, limited liability (general) partnerships, electing partnerships that are not LPs, LPs (including LLLPs), professional associations and business trusts, plus the foreign versions of business corporations, nonprofit corporations, LLCs, LPs (including LLLPs), LLGPs, professional associations and business trusts.
pa_facts.quote: Beginning in 2025, most domestic and foreign filing associations are required to file an Annual Report [DSCB:15-146].
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The Department's official forms notice in the Pennsylvania Bulletin lists the domestic and foreign association types that must file annual reports.
pa_facts.value: business corporations; nonprofit corporations; LLCs; LPs; LLGPs; electing partnerships; professional associations; business trusts
pa_facts.quote: The types of domestic and foreign associations that must file an annual report include: business corporations; nonprofit corporations; limited liability companies; limited partnerships; limited liability general partnerships; electing partnerships; professional associations; and business trusts.
pa_facts.source_title: 54 Pa.B. 8207 (Dec. 14, 2024), Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations; Proposed Official Forms

pa_facts.claim: Limited liability limited partnerships (LLLPs), domestic and foreign, file as limited partnerships and fall under the LP category, with a December 31 deadline.
pa_facts.quote: Domestic limited partnerships (including limited liability limited partnerships)
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: These filing types do not have to file annual reports: fictitious names, general partnerships that are not LLPs, authorities, name reservations, land banks, financial institutions and credit unions, name registrations, trademarks, and insignias/marks.
pa_facts.quote: Filing types that are not required to make Annual Reports are: fictitious names, general partnerships that are not limited liability partnerships, authorities (all subtypes), name reservations, land banks, financial institutions and credit unions, name registrations, trademarks, insignias and marks used with articles and supplies.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Entities showing any 'Inactive' status (dissolved, terminated, merged out, withdrawn, cancelled) do not file annual reports. Any entity with an 'Active' status must file.
pa_facts.quote: If the association status is “Active” or any variation thereof on the Department’s website, annual reports are required.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: All corporations (business and nonprofit, domestic and foreign) must file by June 30 each year.
pa_facts.quote: For all corporations (business and nonprofit, domestic and foreign), the deadline is June 30 of each year.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: LLCs, domestic and foreign, must file by September 30 each year.
pa_facts.quote: The deadline for limited liability companies (domestic and foreign) is September 30, and the annual report of any other domestic filing entity or foreign filing association is due on or before December 31 of each year.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Every other association type (LPs, LLLPs, LLPs/LLGPs, electing partnerships, business trusts, professional associations), domestic and foreign, must file on or before December 31 each year.
pa_facts.quote: The deadline for limited liability companies (domestic and foreign) is September 30, and the annual report of any other domestic filing entity or foreign filing association is due on or before December 31 of each year.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The statute phrases the deadlines as: before July 1 for corporations (profit or nonprofit), before October 1 for LLCs, and on or before December 31 for every other domestic or foreign association.
pa_facts.quote: (1) before July 1 in the case of a domestic or foreign corporation for profit or not-for-profit; (2) before October 1 in the case of a domestic or foreign limited liability company; and (3) on or before December 31 in the case of any other form of domestic or foreign association.

pa_facts.claim: Each type's filing window opens January 1 of the report year and runs to its deadline: corporations Jan 1–June 30, LLCs Jan 1–Sept 30, all others Jan 1–Dec 31.
pa_facts.quote: The filing window is based on the entity type: corporations Jan. 1 – June 30; limited liability companies Jan. 1 – Sept. 30; and all others Jan. 1 – Dec. 31.
pa_facts.source_title: Department of State Alerts Business Owners About New Annual Report Requirement Starting in 2025

pa_facts.claim: The annual report fee is $7 for business corporations, LLCs, LPs and LLGPs.
pa_facts.quote: The fee is $7 for business corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs), limited partnerships (LPs) and limited liability general partnerships (LLPs).
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Nonprofit corporations, and LPs or LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose, pay no annual report fee.
pa_facts.quote: There is no fee for nonprofit corporations and any LPs or LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The statutory fee schedule, 15 Pa.C.S. § 153(a)(18), covers both domestic and foreign associations: $0 for nonprofit corporations and for LPs/LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose, and $7 otherwise, whether filed electronically or on paper. (Dot leaders shortened in the quote.)
pa_facts.quote: (18) Annual report of domestic or foreign association: (i) Annual report delivered to the bureau by a nonprofit corporation or a limited partnership or limited liability company with a not-for-profit purpose... 0 (ii) Annual report delivered to the bureau electronically... 7 (iii) Annual report not delivered to the bureau electronically... 7
pa_facts.effective_date: Act 122 of 2022, eff. 60 days after Nov. 3, 2022
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 153. Fee schedule

pa_facts.claim: Domestic and foreign associations pay the same annual report fee. The § 153(a)(18) entry covers the 'annual report of domestic or foreign association' and does not set a separate foreign rate.
pa_facts.quote: (18) Annual report of domestic or foreign association:
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 153. Fee schedule

pa_facts.claim: The official paper form DSCB:15-146 says the $7 fee also applies to business trusts and any other for-profit association, and that $0 applies to nonprofit corporations and any other not-for-profit association. (The dash is rendered as an unmappable glyph in the PDF.)
pa_facts.quote: $7 – filed by a corporation, limited liability company, limited partnership, limited liability general partnership, business trust or other association with a for-profit purpose $0 – filed by a non-profit corporation or other association with a not-for-profit purpose
pa_facts.source_title: DSCB:15-146 Annual Report form

pa_facts.claim: Veteran- or reservist-owned businesses get no annual report fee waiver.
pa_facts.quote: Is there a fee waiver for the annual report for a veteran- or reservist-owned business? No.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The annual report requirement started January 1, 2025, so 2025 was the first year reports were due.
pa_facts.quote: The annual report requirement begins on January 1, 2025.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Section 146 took effect January 3, 2024. Reports begin in the calendar year after an entity becomes subject to the section, which made January 1, 2025 the first reporting year.
pa_facts.quote: Section 5 of Act 122 (relating to annual reports) became effective January 3, 2024. Under 15 Pa.C.S. § 146(c) and (h) (relating to annual report), annual reports begin with the calendar year after which an entity or association first becomes subject to this section, for example, January 1, 2025.

pa_facts.claim: A company does not file an annual report in the calendar year it is formed or first registers as a foreign entity. Its first report is due the following year.
pa_facts.quote: No. A company’s first annual report is due the year following its formation in Pennsylvania or its initial foreign registration.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: No dissolution, termination or cancellation applies to 2025 or 2026 reports. Starting with reports due in 2027, an entity that does not file becomes subject to administrative dissolution, termination or cancellation six months after its due date.
pa_facts.quote: Beginning with Annual Reports due in 2027, associations that fail to file annual reports in the 2027 calendar year will be subject to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the due date of the Annual Report.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Under 15 Pa.C.S. § 381, DOS may start administrative dissolution of a domestic filing entity (or cancellation of an LLP registration or electing-partnership statement) if the report is not filed within six months after its due date. This applies only to reports due on or after January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.quote: if the entity does not deliver an annual report to the department within six months after the annual report is due. (b) Transitional provision.--Subsection (a) applies with respect to annual reports due on or after January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 381. Grounds for administrative dissolution or cancellation

pa_facts.claim: Under 15 Pa.C.S. § 419, DOS may terminate a registered foreign association's registration if it does not file an annual report within six months after it is due. This ground applies to reports due on or after January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.quote: (3) has failed to deliver to the department for filing an annual report under section 146 (relating to annual report) within six months after it is due. ... (e) Transitional provision.--Subsection (a)(3) shall apply with respect to annual reports due on or after January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 419. Termination of registration

pa_facts.claim: Act 20 of 2024 (HB 1419, signed June 10, 2024, effective immediately) pushed the start of foreign-registration termination for missed annual reports from reports due on or after January 3, 2026 to reports due on or after January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.quote: (e) Transitional provision.--Subsection (a)(3) shall apply with respect to annual reports due on or after [January 3, 2026] January 4, 2027.
pa_facts.source_title: Act of Jun. 10, 2024, P.L. 381, No. 20

pa_facts.claim: Act 122 builds in a transition period with no dissolution, termination or cancellation for missed 2025 and 2026 reports. After that, the entity has six months past the due date before DOS may act, plus the statutory notice periods.
pa_facts.value: 2025-2026 reports: no dissolution; 2027+: 6 months after due date (plus >=60-day notice)
pa_facts.quote: Therefore, Act 122 requires that the Department provide associations with a transition period before imposing any dissolution/termination/cancellation for failure to file Annual Reports.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Before dissolving a domestic entity or cancelling an LLP or electing partnership, DOS must send a notice. The entity then has 60 days to file the missing report or show it was filed. The dissolution effective date must be at least 60 days after the notice is delivered.
pa_facts.quote: If an entity does not deliver to the department for filing, within 60 days after delivery of the notice required by subsection (a), the required annual report or demonstrate to the satisfaction of the department that the annual report was delivered to the department, the department must:
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 382. Procedure and effect

pa_facts.claim: A foreign registration termination takes effect no less than 60 days after DOS delivers notice. It does not happen if the association cures every ground for termination before that date.
pa_facts.value: notice + >=60 days; cure allowed before effective date
pa_facts.quote: The registration of a registered foreign association to do business in this Commonwealth shall cease on the effective date of the notice of termination or notation under subsection (b), unless before that date the association cures each ground for termination stated in the notice or notation.
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 419. Termination of registration

pa_facts.claim: Not filing leads to administrative dissolution for domestic filing entities, administrative cancellation for domestic LLPs, or administrative termination for foreign associations, and loss of name protection, beginning with reports not filed in 2027.
pa_facts.quote: Failure to file the annual report will subject the association to (i) administrative dissolution if it is a domestic filing entity, (ii) administrative cancellation if it is a domestic limited liability partnership; or (iii) administrative termination of its registration if it is a foreign association and loss of the protection of its name beginning with annual reports not filed in 2027.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Once DOS files the dissolution, cancellation or termination statement, the association cannot get a subsistence certificate and other associations may use its name.
pa_facts.quote: After a Statement of Administrative Dissolution, Cancellation of Registration or Termination of Foreign Registration is filed, the association will not be able to obtain a subsistence certificate and its name becomes available for use by other associations.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: An administratively dissolved domestic entity keeps existing but may only wind up and liquidate or apply for reinstatement. Its governors keep managing it, and it is not considered subsisting.
pa_facts.quote: continues its existence as the same type of entity but may not carry on any activities except as necessary to wind up its activities and affairs and liquidate its assets in the manner provided in its organic law or to apply for reinstatement under section 383 (relating to reinstatement);

pa_facts.claim: When a domestic LLP's or electing partnership's registration or election is cancelled, it continues as a general partnership and loses LLP/electing-partnership status (and its limited liability).
pa_facts.quote: A domestic limited liability partnership or electing partnership that is not also a limited partnership and whose statement of registration or statement of election is administratively canceled continues its existence as a general partnership but not as a limited liability partnership or electing partnership.

pa_facts.claim: No separate late-filing fee was found. The § 153 fee schedule lists only the $0/$7 annual report fees and reinstatement fees. The only extra charge for missed reports is $15 per unpaid report, paid as part of reinstatement. This conclusion rests on the absence of a late fee, not on an explicit statement.
pa_facts.quote: (iii) Additional fee required by section 383(a)(4)(ii) (relating to reinstatement) for each annual report not previously paid... 15

pa_facts.claim: Reinstatement for domestic filing associations and LLPs/electing partnerships costs $35 online or $40 on paper, plus $15 for each missing annual report.
pa_facts.quote: The fees for reinstatement are Application for Reinstatement filed online - $35 Application for Reinstatement filed on paper - $40 Additional fee for each missing annual report - $15
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The statutory reinstatement fees match: $35 electronic, $40 paper, and $15 for each annual report not previously paid.
pa_facts.quote: (19) Reinstatement of domestic association: (i) Application for reinstatement delivered to the bureau electronically... 35 (ii) Application for reinstatement not delivered to the bureau electronically... 40

pa_facts.claim: A dissolved domestic entity, LLP or electing partnership can apply for reinstatement at any time; there is no time limit. The application must include the reinstatement fee and a fee for each unpaid report, and the entity keeps its original entity number.
pa_facts.quote: it has the opportunity for reinstatement, with no limitation on the period of time for such reinstatement. Such reinstatement must be accompanied by the application for reinstatement fee and a fee for each delinquent annual report that was not previously paid. The reinstated domestic filing entity or partnership will keep the same entity number/file number
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Under § 383, the reinstatement application must attach the most recent unfiled annual report and the fees for every report that should have been paid. DOS then files a statement of reinstatement within 30 days of receiving the application.
pa_facts.value: attach_latest_report + all_missed_fees; DOS acts within 30 days
pa_facts.quote: (ii) that the most recent annual report not previously filed is attached to the application for reinstatement along with the fee for each of the annual reports that should have been paid under section 153.
pa_facts.source_title: 15 Pa.C.S. § 383. Reinstatement

pa_facts.claim: Reinstatement relates back to the dissolution or cancellation date, except for the name (if someone else took it in the meantime) and the rights of anyone who relied on the dissolution.
pa_facts.quote: Reinstatement for domestic filing entities and limited liability/electing partnerships is effective as of the date of the administrative dissolution or cancellation, except as to: Use of the entity’s name, if someone else registered the name in the interim; or The rights of anyone who relied on the administrative dissolution or cancellation
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: A foreign association whose registration is terminated for not filing cannot reinstate. It must re-register by filing a new Foreign Registration Statement and gets a new entity number. Re-registration is not retroactive.
pa_facts.quote: If a registered foreign association discovers that its foreign registration has been terminated for failure to file an annual report, the foreign association may not cure retroactively by reinstating, but instead must reregister by submitting a new Foreign Registration Statement. The reregistered foreign company will receive a new entity number/file number with the Department of State.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The statutory fee for a foreign registration statement is $250. It is inferred, not stated by DOS, that a terminated foreign entity re-registering by filing a new Foreign Registration Statement pays this fee.
pa_facts.quote: (2) Foreign associations: (i) Registration statement or similar qualifications to do business... 250

pa_facts.claim: Foreign PLLCs, LLLPs and LLPs/LLGPs cannot reinstate either. Their activities between termination and re-registration are not validated, and their liability shield is not restored retroactively.
pa_facts.quote: Unlike domestic PLLCs, LLLPs and LLPs/LLGPs, the activities of the foreign association between the date of its administrative termination and the date it files a new Foreign Registration Statement are not valid as if the administrative termination had never occurred. Furthermore, the liability shield for foreign LLLPs and LLPs/LLGPs is not retroactively reinstated.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: While an entity is dissolved, terminated or cancelled, other associations can take its name. If one does, the returning entity must choose a new name.
pa_facts.quote: During the time of administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation, the association’s name (domestic or foreign) is made available to any other filing association.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: DOS mails a postcard notice to the registered office at least two months before each deadline (CROPs get Excel lists instead), and sends courtesy emails to addresses on file. Not receiving a notice does not excuse the filing.
pa_facts.value: notice >= 2 months before due date; non-receipt no excuse
pa_facts.quote: The department annually must deliver notice to each association required to file an annual report under this section of the annual report filing requirement at least two months before the annual report is due. Failure by the department to deliver notice to any party, or failure by any party to receive notice, of an annual report filing requirement does not relieve the party of the obligation

pa_facts.claim: The report must state: name and jurisdiction of formation; registered office address (or CROP); at least one governor; principal officers' names and titles, if any; principal office address; and the DOS entity number. No financial information is required.
pa_facts.quote: Is any financial information required on the annual report? No.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Information in the report must be current as of the filing date, not as of the prior calendar year.
pa_facts.quote: (b) Date of information.--Information in an annual report must be current as of the date the report is delivered to the department for filing.

pa_facts.claim: A filed report can be updated free of charge until the end of the calendar year it was filed, using the Annual Report Update (Change in Information) form DSCB:15-146(f). The update needs PIN access to the entity.
pa_facts.quote: An association may update or change information previously included in a filed annual report at any time after filing until the end of the calendar year which the annual report was filed.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Online filings at file.dos.pa.gov are approved automatically and immediately, and no PIN is needed to file. There is no expedited option. Paper filings are date-stamped on receipt, processed in the regular queue and returned by mail.
pa_facts.quote: In addition, Annual Reports submitted online will be automatically approved. Online filers see statuses in real time and will be able to access the approved Annual Report within minutes. Therefore, there are no expedited service options for Annual Reports.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The annual report does not replace the Certificate of Annual Registration (CAR). LLPs, LLLPs and restricted professional companies (PLLCs), domestic or foreign, must still file the CAR by April 15 each year.
pa_facts.quote: The Certificate of Annual Registration (CAR) form and the corresponding annual registration fee are not replaced by the Annual Report and must be filed on or before April 15 of each year.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: Act 122 repealed the old decennial report requirement for associations.
pa_facts.quote: The new Annual Report filing begins in calendar year 2025. The long-time decennial report requirement has been repealed.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

pa_facts.claim: The Annual Report (form DSCB:15-146) is meant to be filed online through the Department of State's Business Filing Services (BFS) portal at file.dos.pa.gov.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
pa_facts.quote: The Annual Report [DSCB:15-146] should be filed online at file.dos.pa.gov.

pa_facts.claim: Official online steps: log in to file.dos.pa.gov, find the entity with Business Search, click the 'File Annual Report' icon (no PIN needed), confirm or update the entity's information, pay the fee ($7, or $0 for nonprofits), and get the filed report within minutes in the My Business Work Queue. There is no separate deep link to the form. You reach it from the entity's search result.
pa_facts.value: file.dos.pa.gov > Business Search > select entity > 'File Annual Report' icon > confirm/update > pay > My Business Work Queue
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
pa_facts.quote: Log in to https://file.dos.pa.gov Search for the company name under Business Search Click on “File Annual Report” icon (no PIN access required) Confirm/update your entity information Pay the $7 fee (no fee for nonprofits) Receive your filed report within minutes under the My Business Work Queue

pa_facts.claim: Filing online requires a Business Filing Services (BFS) user account. New users must register, then log in at file.dos.pa.gov.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
pa_facts.quote: Register an account for Business Filing Services (BFS) if you are new user (Customer Portal Overview). Log in at file.dos.pa.gov and search for your company name under "Business Search."

pa_facts.claim: Logging in to BFS goes through the PA Business Hub (hub.business.pa.gov), which uses Keystone Login. In the official guide, Step 1 is to click Login at file.dos.pa.gov and Step 2 is to sign in or register at hub.business.pa.gov. An existing Keystone Login from another Commonwealth system can be reused.
pa_facts.source_title: How to File an Annual Report in Business Filing Services (PA DOS guide)
pa_facts.quote: Go to https://hub.business.pa.gov/. Enter your username and password. Click Log in. New users should register for an account by clicking the Register button on the right. ... NOTE: The Business Hub utilizes Keystone Login. If you have an existing Keystone Login from another Commonwealth system associated with your email address, use your existing information to Log in.

pa_facts.claim: Anyone can browse the BFS portal without logging in, but the portal asks for a login before any filing action. (This comes from an older DOS Customer Portal Overview guide that still refers to corporations.pa.gov.)
pa_facts.source_title: Customer Portal Overview (PA DOS BFS guide)
pa_facts.quote: A user can navigate the website prior to logging in but will be prompted to login if executing an action such as filing.

pa_facts.claim: The PA Business Hub has an official 'File an Annual Report' Quick Action page. It names DOS Business Filing Services as the system and form DSCB:15-146, then sends the user on to BFS ('Continue to BFS').
pa_facts.source_title: Quick Action - PA Business Hub (File an Annual Report)
pa_facts.quote: File an Annual Report By clicking a link below, you may leave the Business Hub. Agency: Department of State System: Business Filing Services Before you start your annual report (DSCB: 15-146), review the helpful information and resources below to make sure you're prepared.

pa_facts.claim: Filing the annual report does not need a PIN or entity-ownership access in BFS. Any logged-in BFS user can open the Annual Report form for an entity found in Business Search.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
pa_facts.quote: Click on the icon for Annual Report. No PIN access is required to file an Annual Report.

pa_facts.claim: The annual report form number is DSCB:15-146. The requirement began in 2025.
pa_facts.source_title: Annual Reports | Department of State | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
pa_facts.quote: Beginning in 2025, most domestic and foreign filing associations are required to file an Annual Report [DSCB:15-146].

pa_facts.claim: The official paper form is DSCB:15-146, edition dated 1/1/2025. It is published as a PDF on pa.gov. The form itself says online filing is the route for immediate processing and that paper forms will not be expedited.

pa_facts.quote: This form may be submitted online at file.dos.pa.gov. If submitting on paper, typewritten is preferred. If handwritten, the form must be legible and completed in black or blue-black ink in order to permit reproduction.

pa_facts.claim: Paper annual reports and payment are mailed to the PA Department of State, Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations, P.O. Box 8722, Harrisburg, PA 17105-8722 (phone (717) 787-1057).

pa_open_questions: Late fee: no official page or statute found imposes a late fee for filing after the deadline but before dissolution. The only monetary consequences found are the $15-per-report fee and the $35/$40 fee at reinstatement. DOS does not say explicitly that no late fee exists; confirm with DOS (717-787-1057, option 5).
Early filing: DOS describes the filing window as Jan 1 through the due date. No source says whether a report can be filed before January 1 for the next year, or whether file.dos.pa.gov blocks that.
Formation year: DOS says an entity is not required to file in its formation or foreign-registration year. No source says whether a voluntary filing in that year is allowed or would count.

Actual enforcement dates are not published. Under 15 Pa.C.S. §§ 381/419 (reports due on or after Jan 4, 2027, plus six months, plus a notice period of at least 60 days), the earliest dates work out to roughly: corporations missing June 30, 2027 -> proceedings from about Jan 2028; LLCs missing Sept 30, 2027 -> about Apr 2028; others missing Dec 31, 2027 -> about July 2028; effective dissolution at least 60 days after notice. These are derived, not stated by DOS.

Missed 2025/2026 reports: § 383(a)(4)(ii) requires the fee for 'each of the annual reports that should have been paid,' and DOS charges $15 per missing report. Unclear whether reports missed in the 2025-2026 transition years count if an entity is later dissolved over a 2027+ report and reinstates.

Missed 2025/2026 reports can never trigger dissolution on their own (enforcement applies only to reports due on or after Jan 4, 2027). No source says whether DOS will require catch-up filing of those reports.

Fee edge case: the statute gives $0 only to nonprofit corporations and to LPs/LLCs with a not-for-profit purpose, but form DSCB:15-146 says $0 for any 'other association with a not-for-profit purpose' (for example a nonprofit business trust or professional association). The statute and form differ for these rare cases.
Typo on the DOS page: an FAQ bullet reads 'Jan. 1 - Dec. 3' for 'all other associations'; the same FAQ's text, the table, and § 146(c)(3) all say December 31. December 31 is treated as correct.
Restricted professional companies/PLLCs are LLCs, so the September 30 deadline and $7 fee presumably apply, but DOS does not state this explicitly for annual reports.
No source addresses whether a due date on a weekend or holiday (for example June 30, 2029, a Saturday) moves to the next business day.

The URL suggested in the task (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/business/annual-reports) returns HTTP 404. The current official page is https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/business/types-of-filings-and-registrations/annual-reports.
The $250 foreign re-registration fee is inferred from the statutory fee for a foreign registration statement (§ 153(a)(2)(i)). DOS does not state it in the annual report context.

Online payment methods beyond 'credit card' could not be confirmed from official pages: debit cards, ACH/e-check, and prepaid or deposit accounts for high-volume filers are all unconfirmed. file.dos.pa.gov returned a 'Security Check' page to automated fetches, so the live checkout screen could not be inspected.

Paper payment is unclear: the DSCB:15-146 instructions mention only checks payable to the PA Department of State, while the general Fees and Payments page also allows money orders. Whether money orders are accepted for paper annual reports specifically is unconfirmed.

No official turnaround time exists for PAPER annual reports. DOS says only that they go into the regular queue and come back by mail. The general figures conflict (15 business days in the business FAQ versus 1-3 business days on the Business Hub page), and neither is annual-report-specific.

The two forms conflict on how to file updates. The DSCB:15-146 instructions say updates to a filed report 'must be made online at file.dos.pa.gov'. The DSCB:15-146(f) Update form says it 'may be mailed' to P.O. Box 8722. It is unclear whether DOS accepts paper updates.

The exact deep link to the annual report form inside BFS could not be verified. Official guidance only describes going through file.dos.pa.gov > Business Search > 'File Annual Report' icon (or the Business Hub Quick Action page).

Keystone Login: current DOS guides route BFS login through hub.business.pa.gov, which uses Keystone Login. The older Customer Portal Overview describes a separate portal account at corporations.pa.gov. Whether any BFS login path exists that skips the Hub/Keystone was not confirmed.

For third-party filers, no official page was found covering: BFS terms of use for agents or filing services, filing for many unrelated entities from one account, or any disclosure a service must make when signing as 'authorized representative'. The DOS scam alerts show DOS expects services to tell customers about the direct $7/$0 option.

It was not confirmed where the BFS entity-access PIN (needed for the Annual Report Update, not for the original report) is emailed, for example to the entity's email on file. That affects whether a third-party service can file updates without the client's help.

The DOS fee schedule lists 'Annual Report - Benefit corporation $70'. Its relationship to the $7 DSCB:15-146 annual report (for example, whether benefit corporations pay an extra or different amount) was not confirmed.

Whether the online e-signature must be given by a governor or officer, or can be given by an agent such as a filing service employee with a title like 'Authorized Agent', is not stated. DOS says it does not examine signer authority (15 Pa.C.S. § 135(a)(7)), and § 135(b) allows signing by attorney-in-fact.

First dissolution dates: § 381(b) applies to annual reports due on or after 2027-01-04, and § 381(a) allows proceedings once a report is six months late. That suggests corporate proceedings could start around the end of 2027 or early 2028 (2027 report due before July 1, 2027), then a 60-day notice period, then an effective date at least 60 days after notice. No official page states actual calendar dates for the first dissolutions. These are inferences only.

The statute sets deadlines as 'before July 1' and 'before October 1', and DOS publishes June 30 and September 30. It is not confirmed whether DOS starts the six-month § 381 clock from June 30/September 30 or from July 1/October 1.

Reinstatement fees: § 153(a)(19)(iii) sets $15 per unpaid annual report as an 'additional fee required by section 383(a)(4)(ii)'. It is not confirmed whether the $15 replaces the $7 fee for each missed report or is charged on top of it. DOS pages list only '$15 for each missing annual report'.

The DOS fee schedule lists 'Annual Report - Benefit corporation $70'. This is probably the separate annual benefit report for benefit corporations under 15 Pa.C.S. Chapter 33, not the § 146 annual report, but no statute section confirming that was fetched in this session.
Act 122's 60-day effective date computes to January 2, 2023. No official page fetched states that calendar date.

Currency: the palegis.us history notes show no amendments to §§ 146, 153, or 381-384 after Act 122 of 2022, and only Act 20 of 2024 for § 419(e). The closest risk is the "Government services" category on Stripe's Prohibited list (page last updated 2026-09-22). stripe.pass_through_fee_guidance:
No Stripe page covers passing government filing fees through at cost. The rules below come from general Stripe terms.

1. It is not a surcharge. Payments Terms §3.4(e) limits fees for accepting payment cards, and the state fee is a cost of the service, not a card fee. Do not add a card-processing or convenience fee unless card network rules and the law allow it, and notify Stripe at least 60 days before you start.

2. Be transparent. §3.7 requires accurately stating the nature and amount of each charge and disclosing material terms before purchase. The Prohibited list also bans unclear or hidden pricing. Before payment, show two line items: the "[State] filing fee (paid to the state at cost)" and "Service fee (our fee)", plus the total. The receipt should repeat the same breakdown, since §2 requires a complete and accurate receipt.

3. Take one charge for the whole service. Your business is the merchant of record and pays the state from its own account. This avoids looking like you collect payments on the state's behalf, which Stripe restricts under payment facilitation and aggregation.

4. Charge the actual state fee. If the state's fee turns out lower, or a late fee applies, refund or collect the difference with the customer's explicit consent.

5. Refunds. Stripe requires a fair and neutral refund policy (§3.8). A reasonable policy: full refund before filing; after filing, the state fee cannot be refunded because it has been paid to the state, and the service fee follows your published policy. Refunds must go back to the original payment method.

6. Evidence for disputes. Keep the customer's authorization, the data they submitted, the time of submission, and the state's confirmation. You are liable for every dispute (§5.2).
recommendations: When activating Stripe, pick an industry that maps to a non-restricted MCC: 7399 Miscellaneous Business Services, 8999 Professional Services, or 7339 Secretarial Support Services. Do not pick Government Services (MCC 9399), which is restricted.

Use a plain onboarding description, for example: 'Private business-compliance service. We prepare and submit state annual reports for small businesses; a staff member files on the state's website. We charge a service fee plus the state filing fee at cost, shown separately. Not a government agency, not affiliated with any state, not a law firm, no legal advice.'

Before launch, ask Stripe Support to confirm eligibility in writing and keep the reply. The General Terms §1.2(a)(ix) refer to written pre-approval, and this business sits next to the prohibited 'Government services' category.

Put a clear non-affiliation disclaimer near the top of the site, at checkout, and in all emails and mailers: private company, not affiliated with or endorsed by any government agency. Consider adding that customers can file directly with the state, usually for just the state fee, with a link to the official Secretary of State site. That strengthens the value-add, not-misleading case.

Avoid anything that looks official: state seals, flags, agency-style names or domains, words like 'Official', 'Department', 'Bureau' or 'Division', notices styled as government mail, urgency or penalty scare tactics, and fake testimonials. These trigger Stripe's misleading-claims and deceptive-practices bans and draw disputes.

Spell out the value you add on the site: preparation and checking of the report, deadline tracking and reminders, a person handling the submission, delivery of the state's confirmation or receipt, and support.
Itemize every charge: state filing fee (at cost, per state), service fee, and total before payment. Repeat the breakdown on the Stripe receipt and in the confirmation email.

Publish a refund and cancellation policy that is fair and neutral. For example: full refund if cancelled before filing; after submission the state fee cannot be refunded; service-fee refund if you make an error or miss the deadline. Link it at checkout.

State and meet a filing turnaround, such as within 2 business days. If you plan to charge well ahead of filing (pre-paid future years or subscriptions charged before the due date), tell Stripe first. Payments Terms §5.3(b) lets Stripe act if you charge for services not immediately deliverable without its consent.
If you offer auto-renewing annual plans, get clear consent at signup, send a reminder before each renewal charge, and make cancelling easy. Stripe prohibits negative-option offers with unclear terms.
Set a statement descriptor based on your brand name (dynamic suffix like 'ANNUAL RPT'). Never use a state or agency name.

Before filing, have the customer authorize the filing and confirm the information is accurate. Keep that consent, the submitted data and the state's confirmation as dispute evidence, and watch your dispute rate.
Pay state fees from your own business account. Do not hold customer money as the state's agent, which could look like restricted payment facilitation.

Tell Stripe before adding new services, such as entity formation, registered agent service, BOI filings or document drafting. Stripe prohibits services not disclosed in the account application, and adding legal-document drafting could raise legal-services questions.

directory.agency_name: Idaho Secretary of State, Business Services Division

directory.name: Indiana
directory.agency_name: Indiana Secretary of State, Business Services Division
directory.notes: The agency page and the INBiz portal (https://inbiz.in.gov/) both refer to filing a 'business entity report'. The public business search loaded in the browser under INBiz branding.

directory.name: Iowa
directory.agency_name: Iowa Secretary of State, Business Services Division
directory.notes: https://sos.iowa.gov/business/ returns 404, so the current page is recorded. 'Biennial Report' is confirmed by the official Secretary of State news page on Fast Track Filing for biennial reports. Online filings go through https://filings.sos.iowa.gov. The search page loaded in the browser as 'Business Entities Search'.

directory.name: Kansas
directory.agency_name: Kansas Secretary of State, Business Services Division
directory.notes: https://sos.ks.gov/business/business.html returns 404, so the current page is recorded. The site uses 'File Information Report' and 'Information Reports' where it formerly said Annual Report. The business search URL is linked from the official page, but it sits behind a human-verification check that was not bypassed, so the search page itself was not seen loading.

directory.name: Kentucky
directory.agency_name: Kentucky Secretary of State - Business Filings
directory.notes: Agency page loaded through WebFetch. It links the business search and says entities must file an annual report. The Annual-Reports.aspx page under the same office also uses 'annual reports'.

directory.name: Louisiana
directory.agency_name: Louisiana Secretary of State - Commercial Division (Business Services)
directory.notes: The old /BusinessServices/Pages/default.aspx URL now returns 404, because the site was restructured to /business-services. directory.name: Maine
directory.agency_name: Maine Secretary of State - Division of Corporations, UCC & Commissions (Bureau of Corporations, Elections & Commissions), Corporations-Business Services
directory.notes: The old URL /sos/cec/corp/index.html redirects here, and /sos/cec/corp/ returns 404. The page links 'File an Annual Report' and 'Annual Reports Online'. The search page loaded with the title 'Search Corporate Names'.

directory.name: Maryland
directory.agency_name: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) - Charter Division / Charter Business Services
directory.notes: The page heading is 'Charter Business Services - SDAT'. It refers to 'Annual Reports' filed alongside Business Personal Property Returns. The entity search is on Maryland Business Express (egov.maryland.gov).

directory.name: Massachusetts
directory.agency_name: Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts - Corporations Division
directory.notes: sec.state.ma.us is behind Incapsula bot protection. It returned an empty challenge page to WebFetch, curl and the browser, and I did not try to get past it, so the fetch is not confirmed. The report name and search URL come from the official mass.gov page 'Starting a corporation in Massachusetts', which loaded in the browser. That page says 'All corporations must file an annual report with the Secretary of the Commonwealth' and links 'search for a Business Entity' to the corp.sec.state.ma.us URL.

directory.name: Michigan
directory.agency_name: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) - Corporations, Securities & Commercial Licensing Bureau, Corporations Division
directory.notes: WebFetch and curl got an Akamai 403, but the page loaded normally in the browser pane as 'Corporations Division'. The page says 'All annual reports and annual statements must now be submitted online'. Generally corporations file annual reports and LLCs file annual statements, but the page does not say which is which. The Business Entity Search link points to the MiBusiness Registry Portal, live since June 23, 2025.

directory.name: Minnesota
directory.agency_name: Minnesota Secretary of State - Business & Liens (Business Services)
directory.notes: sos.state.mn.us redirects to sos.mn.gov. WebFetch and curl were sent to a Radware bot check, but the agency page loaded normally in the browser pane. A later subpage showed a CAPTCHA, which I did not solve. The official Business Filings Online portal (mblsportal.sos.mn.gov) loaded and lists 'New Business, Amendment, Annual Renewal or Reinstatement'.

directory.name: Mississippi
directory.agency_name: Mississippi Secretary of State - Business Services & External Affairs Division
directory.notes: The old /business-services URL returns a 301 to /business-services-external-affairs. The page links 'Annual Reports' (/business-services/annual-reports) and the Business Search portal. curl got an Akamai 403 on the corp.sos.ms.gov search URL, but it is linked from the official page.

directory.name: Missouri
directory.agency_name: Missouri Secretary of State - Business Services Division (Corporations Unit)
directory.notes: The agency page loaded through WebFetch. curl got a Cloudflare challenge, which I did not try to get past. The official page https://www.sos.mo.gov/fileonline/reports, titled 'Annual and Biennial Registration Reports', uses 'Annual Report', 'Biennial Report' and 'Registration Reports'. The SOS guide is titled 'Filing an Annual or Biennial Registration Report'.

directory.name: Montana
directory.agency_name: Montana Secretary of State - Business Services (Business & UCC Services)
directory.notes: The page references 'Annual Report filing' and links the biz.sosmt.gov filing portal and business search.

directory.name: Nebraska
directory.agency_name: Nebraska Secretary of State - Business Services Division
directory.periodic_report_name: Biennial Report / Biennial Occupation Tax Report
directory.notes: https://sos.nebraska.gov/business-services redirects to this URL. The official page /business-services/annualbiennial-reporting uses 'biennial occupation tax reports' for business corporations and 'biennial reports' for LLCs and nonprofits. It uses 'annual reports' for LLPs and 'annual benefit report' for benefit corporations. The search page loaded with the title 'Corporations and Charities System'.

directory.name: Nevada
directory.agency_name: Nevada Secretary of State - Commercial Recordings Division
directory.notes: The main page https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/businesses is behind Incapsula bot protection, which blocked WebFetch, curl and the browser. I did not try to get past it. I recorded the official 'Nevada Secretary of State Business Hub' (bizhub.nv.gov) instead, which loaded in the browser. Its glossary defines 'Annual List' as the filing that updates officers, directors and managers. esos.nv.gov and nvsilverflume.gov now redirect to ORION, 'Nevada's Business Portal' (orion.nv.gov), which has 'Search Business Entities'. The division name 'Commercial Recordings' was not shown on any page I fetched.

directory.name: New Hampshire
directory.agency_name: New Hampshire Secretary of State - Corporation Division
directory.notes: The old URL /corporation-ucc-securities/corporation is gone ('Page Not Found'). WebFetch and curl got an Akamai 403, but the page loaded normally in the browser pane. It names the 'Secretary of State's Corporation Division' and links 'File Your Annual Report'. Its 'Business Search' link goes to NH QuickStart at the recorded URL.

directory.name: New Jersey
directory.agency_name: New Jersey Department of the Treasury - Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services (DORES)
directory.notes: The page says 'File your Business Annual Report'. The business search is on njportal.com, the State's official online services portal, which is linked from the DORES page even though it is a .com domain. That page loaded as 'Business Entity Name Search'. The DORES page also links a separate Business Records Service at https://www.njportal.com/DOR/businessrecords/.

directory.name: New Mexico
directory.agency_name: New Mexico Secretary of State - Business Services Division
directory.notes: The Business Services page does not name a periodic report. 'Biennial Report' is taken from an official sos.nm.gov press release headline (2018-02-15) about helping businesses file biennial reports on time. It applies to business corporations; nonprofits appear to file an 'Annual Report', but no fetched official page confirmed that. Filings go through the enterprise.sos.nm.gov portal, and the search page title is 'Secretary of State - New Mexico Business Portal'.

directory.name: New York
directory.agency_name: New York Department of State - Division of Corporations, State Records and Uniform Commercial Code
directory.notes: The old URL dos.ny.gov/corporations-state-records-and-ucc returns 404. The official page /biennial-statements-business-corporations-and-limited-liability-companies uses 'Biennial Statement' for business corporations and LLCs. The official link dos.ny.gov/corporation-and-business-entity-database redirects (302) to apps.dos.ny.gov/publicInquiry/.

directory.name: North Carolina
directory.agency_name: North Carolina Department of the Secretary of State - Business Registration Division
directory.notes: The page has a 'File Your Business Annual Report' button. The business search URL is linked from the sosnc.gov homepage. When fetched directly, that search page returned a Cloudflare challenge, which I did not try to get past.

directory.name: North Dakota
directory.agency_name: North Dakota Secretary of State - Business Services
directory.notes: Most filings are done through the FirstStop Portal (firststop.sos.nd.gov). The official Maintain Registration page (sos.nd.gov/business/business-services/maintain-registration) says most businesses must file an 'annual report'. The 'Biennial Reports' link on the site is the office's own agency report, not an entity filing.

directory.name: Ohio
directory.agency_name: Ohio Secretary of State - Business Services Division
directory.notes: On 2026-09-27 every ohiosos.gov host I tried (www.ohiosos.gov, businesssearch.ohiosos.gov, bsportal.ohiosos.gov, and ohiobusinesscentral.gov, which redirects there) returned HTTP 403 with a page titled 'Ohio Secretary of State's Office Website Maintenance'. The agency URL is the known official domain but could not be confirmed. The expected entity search URL is https://businesssearch.ohiosos.gov/, left blank because it is unconfirmed. Periodic report name is not confirmed. Re-check when the site is back up.

directory.name: Oklahoma
directory.agency_name: Oklahoma Secretary of State - Business Filing Department

The Business Filing Department handles corporation, LP, LLC, LLP, general partnership fictitious name, trade name and trademark filings. The entity search page (Search Corporation Entities) was fetched and confirmed.

directory.name: Oregon
directory.agency_name: Oregon Secretary of State - Corporation Division
directory.notes: The official page links 'Renew a Business (File Annual Reports)'. The advanced business name search is linked from the official page. Direct fetches of the search can hit a captcha.

directory.name: Pennsylvania
directory.agency_name: Pennsylvania Department of State - Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations
directory.notes: The official DOS business page refers to 'annual reports in PA'. The business search at file.dos.pa.gov (Business Filing Services) is linked from the official page. Direct fetches of the search hit a security check page.

directory.name: Rhode Island
directory.agency_name: Rhode Island Department of State - Business Services Division
directory.notes: The official page lists a 'Business Annual Report' and a 'Non-Profit Annual Report'. The division maintains the state business registry.

directory.name: South Carolina
directory.agency_name: South Carolina Secretary of State - Business Filings Division
directory.notes: The official SOS FAQ (sos.sc.gov/faqs-about-business-entities) says 'Business corporations must submit the names of directors on Annual Reports filed with the Department of Revenue'. So the corporate annual report is filed with SC DOR, not the Secretary of State. No SOS periodic report for LLCs or nonprofits was confirmed. Search is Business Entities Online (businessfilings.sc.gov); the ExistingFiling link redirects to /Entity/Search.

directory.name: South Dakota
directory.agency_name: South Dakota Secretary of State - Business Services Division
directory.notes: The official page lists 'File an Annual Report'. Name availability, registered agent and trademark searches are also available on sosenterprise.sd.gov.

directory.name: Tennessee
directory.agency_name: Tennessee Secretary of State - Division of Business and Charitable Organizations
directory.notes: WebFetch got a 403 but a curl fetch loaded 'Businesses | Tennessee Secretary of State'. The page says annual reports are filed through the TNCaB system (tncab.tnsos.gov), which requires an account. The division name was confirmed via sos.tn.gov search results.

directory.name: Texas
directory.agency_name: Texas Secretary of State - Business and Government Filings Division
directory.periodic_report_name: Franchise Tax Report / Public Information Report
directory.notes: The official SOS Formation FAQs say for-profit corporations, LLCs and certain LPs file annual franchise tax reports, including a Public Information Report (PIR), with the Comptroller of Public Accounts, not the SOS. Nonprofit corporations, and LPs not subject to franchise tax, file a 'Periodic Report' with the SOS on notice (at most every four years; Form 802 for nonprofits). LLPs file an 'annual report' with the SOS. The search is SOSDirect, which is fee-based. The SOS page announces SOSPortal launching September 29, 2026 to replace SOSDirect and SOSUpload, so the search URL may change.

directory.name: Utah
directory.agency_name: Utah Department of Commerce - Division of Corporations & Commercial Code
directory.notes: corporations.utah.gov 301-redirects to commerce.utah.gov/corporations/. The official page uses 'File an Annual Report/Renewal on an Existing Business', and the renewal-process page treats 'annual report' and 'renewal' as the same filing. The official page links businessregistration.utah.gov as the Business Entity Search. Direct fetches of that site hit a Cloudflare challenge. The deeper path /EntitySearch/OnlineEntitySearch was not confirmed.

directory.name: Vermont
directory.agency_name: Vermont Secretary of State - Business Services Division
directory.notes: The old path sos.vermont.gov/corporations/ now returns 404; the current page is sos.vermont.gov/business-services. The official page lists 'Annual/Biennial Reports', so the report is annual or biennial depending on entity type; the page does not say which types file which. The search on bizfilings.vermont.gov (Online Business Service Center) was fetched and confirmed.

directory.name: Virginia
directory.agency_name: Virginia State Corporation Commission - Office of the Clerk
directory.notes: The old path scc.virginia.gov/business-entities/ returns 404; the current page is scc.virginia.gov/businesses/. The official page mentions both 'annual report' and 'annual registration fees'. It does not say which entity types owe which; my understanding is that corporations file annual reports while LLCs and LPs pay only the annual registration fee, but that was not confirmed. The Clerk's Information System (CIS) is at cis.scc.virginia.gov. The EntitySearch path redirects to a cookie-consent page on the same official domain.

directory.name: Washington
directory.agency_name: Washington Secretary of State - Corporations & Charities Division
directory.notes: The official page references Annual Reports and Initial Reports. Search is the Corporations and Charities Filing System (CCFS). The official page links ccfs.sos.wa.gov/#/, #/AdvancedSearch, and an Express Annual Report search.

directory.agency_name: West Virginia Secretary of State - Business Division

directory.agency_name: Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions - Division of Corporate & Consumer Services

directory.name: Wyoming
directory.agency_name: Wyoming Secretary of State - Business Division
